coverageDimensions: SERVICE coverage would mean: which AWS services Macie can inspect for sensitive data (S3 being the obvious one). This page gives you NOTHING. It never names a single scannable AWS service. The only non-Macie service names anywhere on it are inside detection names — Google Cloud API key, Stripe API key — and those are the things being FOUND in data, not services being scanned. Do not infer service coverage from them. REGION coverage would mean: in which AWS Regions Macie and these managed data identifiers are available. This page gives you NOTHING, and it actively baits you into thinking otherwise, because a column is literally headed 'Countries and regions'. Those are geopolitical countries and regions the identifier formats are designed for. There is no AWS Region name on the page and no per-Region availability statement. RESOURCE TYPE coverage would mean: which resource types Macie inspects (S3 buckets, S3 objects, table buckets) and which file and storage formats it can parse. This page gives you NOTHING — no resource type, no file format, no object type appears. What the page DOES give is two different things that must not be relabelled as any of the above: a detection catalogue (166 managed data identifier IDs grouped into 40 sensitive data types, where 100% is true by construction and no ratio is meaningful), and one genuine external axis — 66 countries and regions whose national data formats Macie can detect, per sensitive data type, with a stated numerator and no stated denominator.

features.reasoning: The managed data identifier ID is the value Macie itself accepts in a job or automated-discovery configuration, so it is the finest-grained unit the page enumerates. It is a CATALOGUE: Macie publishes this list about itself, so 166/166 is true by construction and no ratio should ever be presented from it. Its value to a coverage map is the membership list (does Macie detect Stripe keys? PuTTY keys? Aadhaar?), not a percentage.
features.scope: Per sensitive data type (each ID sits in exactly one row, except 7 IDs that appear in two rows)
features.statuses: All 166 supported, 0 not supported. Every ID on the page is one Macie provides — the intro says the table 'lists all the managed data identifiers that Macie currently provides'. There is no support column, no negative sentence, and nothing marked retired or deprecated. Counted mechanically off the ID column: 173 ID mentions across the 40 rows, minus 7 that appear twice, gives 166 distinct IDs. The 7 repeats are FRANCE_BANK_ACCOUNT_NUMBER, GERMANY_BANK_ACCOUNT_NUMBER, ITALY_BANK_ACCOUNT_NUMBER, SPAIN_BANK_ACCOUNT_NUMBER and UK_BANK_ACCOUNT_NUMBER (in both the BBAN row and the IBAN row), CHILE_RUT_NUMBER and ITALY_NATIONAL_IDENTIFICATION_NUMBER (in both the National identification number row and the Taxpayer identification row). Per-row ID counts: 32 rows carry 1 ID; the multi-ID rows are IBAN 52, Driver's license 32, Taxpayer identification 19, National identification 10, Health insurance/medical ID 6, Passport 7, Phone 7, BBAN 5, and 2 each for Credit card number, Mailing address, Social Security number.

features.featureName: Managed data identifiers by type (sensitive data type)
features.reasoning: The row label is the coarser unit AWS itself organises the page by ('organized by sensitive data type'), and it is the level a human reasons at — 'does Macie find passport numbers?' Also a CATALOGUE: Macie chose these 40 groupings, so 40/40 is definitional. Kept separate from the ID axis because the two lists differ (40 vs 166) and conflating them is the most common counting error on this page.
features.scope: Sensitive data category — Credentials 9, Financial information 7, Personal information: PHI 7, Personal information: PII 17 (sums to 40)
features.statuses: All 40 supported, 0 not supported. Confirmed by counting table rows: 42 lines begin with a pipe, minus the header and separator, equals 40 data rows. The three rows carrying a stated condition rather than unconditional support are Full name ('Any, if the name uses a Latin character set'), GPS coordinates ('Any, if the coordinates are in proximity of an English keyword') and VIN ('Any, if the VIN is in proximity of a keyword in one of the following languages: English, French, German, Lithuanian, Polish, Portuguese, Romanian, or Spanish'). These are qualified support, not exclusions from the list.

features.featureName: Countries and regions (for which managed data identifiers are designed)
features.reasoning: Countries exist whether or not Macie does, so this is the one genuinely EXTERNAL axis on the page and the only place a real coverage gap can be expressed — Macie has a driver's-license identifier for 32 countries and, by silence, none for the rest of the world. Note the second dimension is essential: 'Canada' is covered for driver's licence, passport, phone, mailing address, bank account, health number, SIN and permanent residence, but a bare country-level claim of 'Macie covers Canada' is meaningless. Also note the values are geopolitical countries and regions, NOT AWS Regions.
features.scope: Per sensitive data type / per managed data identifier ID — the column is read per row, not page-wide
features.statuses: 66 distinct named values are stated as covered by at least one identifier. NOT-covered values are not enumerated anywhere: the denominator is the world's countries, and the page never lists the ones Macie has no identifier for. So this axis has a stated numerator and no stated denominator. Counted by splitting the Countries and regions column on commas across the 34 rows that name specific places, then de-duplicating: 66 values, of which 65 are countries or territories and one ('EU', in the Health insurance or medical identification number row) is a supranational region. The other 15 rows say 'Any' (12 unconditional, 3 with a stated condition) and contribute no country values. Widest per-row coverage: IBAN 52 places, Driver's license 32, Taxpayer identification 13.

pageTitle: Quick reference: Managed data identifiers by type
shouldNotExtract: The four intro bullets are a column legend explaining what each column means — they are prose about the table, not data in it. The three cross-links in that legend point to DIFFERENT lists that live on other pages and must not be synthesised here: 'Managed data identifiers recommended for sensitive data discovery jobs' (discovery-jobs-mdis-recommended.md), 'Default settings for automated sensitive data discovery' (discovery-asdd-settings-defaults.md), and 'Keyword requirements' (managed-data-identifiers-keywords.md). The 'See also' section in full, including the appended boilerplate bullet about AWS skills for AI coding assistants and the `aws agent-toolkit search-skills --search-query macie` command — that is AWS page furniture, not Macie capability. The `<a name="mdis-reference-quick">` anchor. The per-row detail-page links (mdis-reference-credentials.md#..., mdis-reference-financial.md#..., mdis-reference-phi.md#..., mdis-reference-pii.md#...) are row identity only, not values. The Sensitive data category column (4 values) is a grouping attribute, not a coverage axis. The Keyword required column (27 Yes, 10 No, 3 Varies) is a detection property, not a support flag. The parentheticals inside the ID column — '(for both Canada and the US)', '(for the US)', '(for the British Virgin Islands)', "(for Brazil's Código de Endereçamento Postal)", '(for credit card numbers in proximity of a keyword)' — are annotations, not identifiers. The 8 languages named in the VIN row are a keyword-proximity condition on one row, not a page-level language axis.
trap: Reading the 'Keyword required' column as a support column. It is a Yes/No/Varies column sitting right next to the country column, so a careless parser produces 10 'not covered' rows — HTTP Basic Authorization header, HTTP cookie, IBAN, JSON Web Token, OpenSSH private key, PGP private key, PKCS private key, PuTTY private key, Stripe API key, Full name — every one of which Macie fully supports. 'No' means no keyword is needed, which is stronger detection, not weaker. Four more traps sit close behind. (1) Counting 40 rows and calling it 40 managed data identifiers; there are 166. (2) Summing per-row IDs to 173 and missing the 7 IDs that appear in two rows. (3) Splitting the country column naively on commas, which turns 'Virgin Islands (British)' and the three 'Any, if ...' conditional cells into junk values, and treats 'Any' as a country. (4) The worst one: mapping the 'Countries and regions' column onto AWS Regions. 'Region' here means a geopolitical region such as the EU. Türkiye, Kosovo and Greenland are not AWS Regions, and this page states nothing whatsoever about AWS Region availability.
whatThePageStates: This is Amazon Macie's single flat index of every managed data identifier it currently provides — the built-in criteria Macie uses to detect a specific type of sensitive data. One table, 40 data rows, five columns: Sensitive data type (linked to a detail page), Sensitive data category, Managed data identifier ID, Keyword required, and Countries and regions. It enumerates what Macie CAN detect and, for country-specific formats, which countries and regions each identifier is designed for. It is purely a catalogue index: there is no Yes/No support column, no unsupported list, and nothing marked retired or deprecated.
